raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #25913.

Loading a PEFT LoRA adapter trained against `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` via `--lora-paths` fails before `/model_info` readiness when the adapter's KV-sharing layers carry `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`o_proj` weights but omit `v_proj`:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to load LoRA adapter ticket-triage: 'base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.15.self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight'
```

The root cause is in `LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj()`. It already zero-filled a missing `k_proj`, but still unconditionally read and popped `v_proj`, so a missing V branch raises a `KeyError`. Reproducing the load on a real Gemma 4 E2B server then surfaces two adjacent native-LoRA gaps that block the same adapter (vision/audio tower wrapping, and wrong per-layer LoRA buffer dims).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora.py`: make qkv normalization symmetric. A missing `k_proj` is zero-filled from `v_proj` when available, otherwise from `q_proj`; a missing `v_proj` is zero-filled from the resolved `k_proj`; and each branch is only popped from the tensor map when it actually existed.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py`: honor `base_model.should_apply_lora(module_name)` in `init_lora_modules()`. This fills in the gate that `init_lora_modules` already referenced in a comment ("... before the should_apply_lora gate, since VL models' should_apply_lora patterns only match language ...") but never actually called, so the method was dead on every model defining it. It is a purely additive skip-only filter: each implementation is a name filter excluding the model's own non-language towers (`qwen2_vl`/`ernie45_vl` skip the `visual`/`vision_model` prefix; `qwen3_vl`/`qwen3_vl_moe`/`qwen2_5_vl`/`mllama4`/`phi4mm`/`gpt_oss`/`qwen3_5`/`gemma3_mm`/`gemma3n_mm`/`gemma4_mm` match a language-tower regex), so a language-only adapter is unaffected (no-op).
- `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py`: derive Gemma 4 multimodal LoRA buffer dims from the text config per layer in `get_hidden_dim()`: `full_attention` layers use `global_head_dim` (512), sliding layers use `swa_head_dim`/`head_dim` (256), and the trailing `num_kv_shared_layers` use the double-wide MLP size. The previous code read these off the top-level multimodal config (which does not carry `intermediate_size`) and asserted a uniform list, allocating wrong shapes and tripping a request-time `o_proj` shape assertion. Also drops a duplicate `get_embed_and_head()` that was shadowed by the later PP-aware definition and dead.

## Accuracy Tests

Real server load on `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` revision `905e84b50c4d2a365ebde34e685027578e6728db` (A800-80GB) with a Gemma 4 PEFT adapter whose layer-15 attention carries `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`o_proj` but no `v_proj` (the reporter's adapter from https://github.com/nemilentsau/sglang-gemma4-triton-fallback):

| case | before fix | after fix |
|---|---|---|
| `--enable-lora --lora-paths ticket-triage=<adapter>` | server **does not start**: `RuntimeError: Failed to load LoRA adapter ticket-triage: '...v_proj.lora_A.weight'` | server **UP** (`/model_info` 200, "fired up"), `/generate` with `lora_path=["ticket-triage"]` returns 200 with a generated token |

Only Gemma 4 is exercised end to end; the other models are covered by the additive, skip-only nature of the `should_apply_lora` gate rather than by new E2E runs. The reporter adapter targets attention only, so the symmetric k-fill path and the double-wide MLP dims are covered by the unit test `test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_qkv_normalization.py` (4 cases).

<details>
<summary>repro (serve command + client + full before/after output)</summary>

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path google/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --context-length 1024 \
  --attention-backend triton --sampling-backend pytorch \
  --enable-lora --lora-paths ticket-triage=<gemma4-e2b-adapter-no-vproj> \
  --max-loras-per-batch 2 --disable-cuda-graph \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.6 --dtype bfloat16

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":["Hello"],"sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":1,"temperature":0},"lora_path":["ticket-triage"]}'
```

before fix (current main): server exits before readiness
```
RuntimeError: Failed to load LoRA adapter ticket-triage: 'base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.15.self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight'
```

after fix:
```
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:30000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
INFO:     127.0.0.1 - "GET /model_info HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
# /generate -> HTTP 200, {"text":"...","output_ids":[9259],...}
```

Environment: A800-80GB, sglang built from this branch, base `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` rev `905e84b50c4d2a365ebde34e685027578e6728db`.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<dev> python -m pytest test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_qkv_normalization.py -q
# 4 passed
```
</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime impact: the changes only run during LoRA adapter loading and model-config-derived dimension setup at startup. The decode path is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

cc @jybsuper

nodes.body:
I tried this branch with a PEFT adapter trained on gemma-4-31B-it and it still fails there, for two reasons that do not show up on E2B:

1. The 31B adapter has v_proj on the 50 sliding layers and no v_proj on the 10 full-attention layers (`attention_k_eq_v`). `normalize_qkv_proj` still decides adapter-wide whether v_proj exists, so it raises the same `KeyError` on layer 5. The new test only covers an adapter with no v_proj anywhere.
2. 31B has `num_global_key_value_heads=4` vs `num_key_value_heads=16`. `get_hidden_dim` uses the global count for every layer, so on sliding layers it allocates a 10240-wide qkv buffer for a 16384-wide tensor. This is the gap @anshulkulhari7 flagged as latent; on 31B it is live.

I also hit a third problem once those two were fixed: PEFT adapters trained on the VLM can carry vision-tower tensors, and `LoRAAdapter` buckets by layer index, so `vision_tower.encoder.layers.N.self_attn.o_proj` overwrote the language o_proj for layer N.

I put the fixes plus a CPU test with the 31B shapes in #40964, on top of the same three changes as this PR, and checked it against HF+PEFT logprobs on the real model. Happy to fold anything back here instead if you would rather land it in this PR.

Thanks @Yash-Sawant22 for running this against a real 31B adapter and confirming the per-layer KV-head sizing gap is live there — that's exactly the asymmetry I flagged in review (`get_hidden_dim` using the global `num_key_value_heads` for every layer while the base `qkv_proj` uses `swa_num_key_value_heads` on sliding layers), and the `getattr(..., "swa_num_key_value_heads", ...)` fallback in #40964 is the same shape I suggested. All three issues stem from treating the adapter as uniform — per-layer presence/sizing for the first two, module-path bucketing for the vision-tower/language `o_proj` collision — so they belong together in that fix. No preference on venue from my side: whichever PR the maintainers want to land it through works, and the 31B-shape CPU test you added is worth keeping either way.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for Gemma 4 multimodal LoRA configurations, updates QKV normalization to handle missing projection branches by zero-filling them, and adds a `should_apply_lora` check during module initialization. It also includes comprehensive unit tests for these changes. The review feedback highlights two critical issues: first, under Grouped Query Attention (GQA), falling back to the Q-projection shape for zero-filling when both K and V projections are missing will cause shape mismatches; second, the new `should_apply_lora` gate will inadvertently skip LoRA for FusedMoE layers on MoE models, requiring special handling for these layers.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Under Grouped Query Attention (GQA), the output dimension of q_proj is different from k_proj and v_proj. If both k_proj and v_proj are missing from the adapter, falling back to weights[q_name] for zero-filling will produce weights with the wrong shape (matching Q instead of KV), leading to shape mismatches and runtime errors. We should compute the correct KV output dimension using the base model's attention configuration when lora_B is being normalized.

```python
                if "k_proj" in target_module:
                    k_proj_weight = weights[k_name]
                elif "v_proj" in target_module:
                    k_proj_weight = torch.zeros_like(weights[v_name])
                else:
                    num_heads = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "num_attention_heads", 1) if self is not None and hasattr(self, "base_hf_config") else 1
                    num_kv_heads = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "num_key_value_heads", num_heads) if self is not None and hasattr(self, "base_hf_config") else 1
                    if "lora_B" in weight_name and num_heads != num_kv_heads:
                        hidden_size = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "hidden_size", 1)
                        head_dim = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "head_dim", hidden_size // num_heads)
                        k_proj_weight = torch.zeros(
                            (num_kv_heads * head_dim, weights[q_name].shape[1]),
                            dtype=weights[q_name].dtype,
                            device=weights[q_name].device,
                        )
                    else:
                        k_proj_weight = torch.zeros_like(weights[q_name])
```

nodes.body:
Thanks for this — it's a careful, well-targeted fix, and the LoRA-side reasoning is genuinely subtle and correct. I read through the diff against `main` (`9bb9d17`) and traced the buffer/slice paths; my overall take is **approve-with-nits**: the core fix is right, the regression test locks in the important case, and the only thing actually keeping it red is a missing CI label, not the code. One real latent correctness gap on a Gemma-4 variant is worth a look but doesn't block the reported #25913 case.

### `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora.py` — the GQA KV zero-fill is exactly right

The both-missing KV-width derivation in `_zero_fill_kv_branch` is subtle but correct. A `q_proj` `lora_B` has out-dim `num_attention_heads * head_dim`, so `q_weight.shape[0] // num_heads` recovers `head_dim` and `* num_kv_heads` gives `num_kv_heads * head_dim` — the true K/V projection width. Deriving `head_dim` from the actual tensor shape rather than a config field is the right call for Gemma, where `head_dim * num_heads != hidden_size` (`head_dim=256`). The `"lora_B" not in weight_name -> zeros_like(q)` short-circuit is also correct, since q/k/v `lora_A` are all `(r, hidden_size)` and thus shape-identical regardless of GQA, and the `num_heads == num_kv_heads` MHA fast-path is correct (KV width == Q width there). This properly addresses the gemini-code-assist GQA concern for the q_proj-only / both-KV-missing case, and `test_missing_k_and_v_use_kv_width_for_lora_b_under_gqa` asserts the V slice is zero at the KV width — which would fail if q's wider output were used — so it actually locks the behavior in. The rewritten `normalize_qkv_proj` (popping k/v only when present, reusing v's shape for missing-k and `zeros_like(k_proj_weight)` for missing-v) is clean and the three test cases cover all three branches.

### `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py` — load-bearing dead-gate fix

This is the quiet but important one. On `main`, `should_apply_lora` is defined on 13 model classes (the VL/audio multimodal models) but has **zero call sites** — the only non-`def` references are the comment at lines 776-778, which already says "before the should_apply_lora gate" even though no gate existed yet. So the method was dead, and every module whose leaf name matched `target_modules` (including vision/audio tower projections) was being wrapped as a LoRA layer. Wiring it via `getattr(self.base_model, "should_apply_lora", None)` is exactly right: text-only models that don't define it get a clean `None` no-op, and the gate is strictly skip-only so it can never wrongly *include* a module. I confirmed the gemma4 `lora_pattern` is anchored on `^language_model\.layers\.`, so `language_model.layers.N.self_attn.qkv_proj` matches while `vision_tower`/`audio_tower`/`embed_vision`/`embed_audio` prefixes don't — towers correctly excluded. Nice catch.

One test-gap note (non-blocking): this gate is now the behavioral core of the lora_manager change, but the new CPU test only exercises `normalize_qkv_proj` and `get_hidden_dim` — nothing touches `init_lora_modules`, and the tower-exclusion is validated only by the single gemma4 E2E run in the description. If it's feasible without a real module map, a small unit test stubbing a `base_model` whose `should_apply_lora` returns `False` for a `vision_tower.*` name and `True` for a `language_model.layers.N.self_attn.qkv_proj` name (then asserting `init_lora_modules` skips the former) would lock the regression in.

### `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py` — root-cause fix is right; one asymmetric-KV gap

Routing `get_hidden_dim` through `get_text_config()` is the right root-cause fix: it reads dims from the same normalized `text_config` that the config normalization mutates (swapping in `global_head_dim` for full-attention, planting `swa_head_dim`) and that the actual `Gemma4TextModel` is built from — instead of the top-level `Gemma4Config` that lacks `intermediate_size` and the per-layer attn dims. The per-layer `head_dim` split (global vs `swa_head_dim`) and the double-wide-MLP tail are handled correctly.

One real latent gap worth a look: `get_hidden_dim` now picks `head_dim` per layer, but the `qkv_proj` branch still uses the **global** `text_config.num_key_value_heads` for *every* layer. The base `qkv_proj` layer uses `swa_num_key_value_heads` on sliding layers (`gemma4_causal.py:308`), and these two diverge whenever `num_global_key_value_heads` is set (`hf_transformers/config.py:167-179`: `num_key_value_heads` becomes the global count, `swa_num_key_value_heads` keeps the raw/sliding count). The LoRA-B buffer is allocated per layer from this `output_dim`, and `slice_lora_b_weights` then slices using the base layer's per-layer KV shard size — so on a Gemma-4 variant where `num_global_key_value_heads != num_key_value_heads`, the sliding-layer qkv buffer width won't match `q + 2*kv` and you'd get a shape error at load. The fix is currently asymmetric: per-layer for `head_dim`, global for the KV-head count. Suggest mirroring the model in the non-`full_attention` branch: `num_kv_heads = getattr(text_config, "swa_num_key_value_heads", text_config.num_key_value_heads)`. This is latent on E2B (equal global/swa KV counts, which is why E2E passes), and the new test uses `num_key_value_heads=1` for both layers so it doesn't exercise it. (`o_proj` is fine since it uses `num_attention_heads`, which is constant across layers.)

### What unblocks this (CI)

The red checks are **not** a real failure. Every failing check is the `run-ci` label gate in `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`: the job exits 1 unless the PR carries the `run-ci` label, and the `*-finish` jobs only go red because they aggregate that gate. This PR currently carries only the `lora` label, so **no actual test/build job has executed** — every GPU/CPU matrix shows `skipping`. That means the new CPU test (`test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_qkv_normalization.py`, registered to `base-a-test-cpu`) hasn't actually run in CI yet, so the current green-ish bits aren't "tests pass." A maintainer needs to add the `run-ci` label to trigger the suites and confirm the new CPU test passes before merge — as an external contributor the author can't add the label or self-trigger.

The repro in the PR body (manual server run + local pytest) is solid; a `run-ci` pass would close the loop. Nice work overall.

---

cc @jybsuper — the only thing keeping this red is the `run-ci` label gate (the PR carries just `lora`, so every suite shows `skipping` and the new CPU test hasn't actually run). Could you add `run-ci` so `base-a-test-cpu` exercises the fix? The one real follow-up I flagged inline — the per-layer `swa_num_key_value_heads` count in `gemma4_mm.get_hidden_dim` — is latent on E2B and doesn't block #25913.

Right — for `gpt_oss` / `qwen3_vl_moe` / `qwen3_5` the patterns already cover `mlp.experts` so the `FusedMoE` branch runs. But `gemma4_mm` was the exception: its `lora_pattern` only had `self_attn|mlp` + `qkv_proj|o_proj|down_proj|gate_up_proj`, so on a gemma4 MoE model (e.g. `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`) `should_apply_lora("language_model.layers.N.mlp.experts")` returned False and the expert module was skipped before the `isinstance(module, FusedMoE)` branch.

Added `mlp.experts` to gemma4's `lora_pattern` in 22d50d0c4c, aligning with the `gpt_oss`/`qwen3_vl_moe` precedent. Verified the pattern now matches `language_model.layers.N.mlp.experts` (and still matches the dense `qkv_proj`/`o_proj`/`gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` paths, no regression).

## Motivation

Fixes #25913.

Loading a PEFT LoRA adapter trained against `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` via `--lora-paths` fails before `/model_info` readiness when the adapter's KV-sharing layers carry `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`o_proj` weights but omit `v_proj`:

Reproducing the load on a real Gemma 4 E2B server then surfaces two adjacent native-LoRA gaps that block the same adapter (vision/audio tower wrapping, and wrong per-layer LoRA buffer dims).

- `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora.py`: make qkv normalization symmetric. A missing `k_proj` is zero-filled from `v_proj` when available, otherwise from `q_proj`; a missing `v_proj` is zero-filled from the resolved `k_proj`; and each branch is only popped from the tensor map when it actually existed.

Also drops a duplicate `get_embed_and_head()` that was shadowed by the later PP-aware definition and dead.

## Accuracy Tests

Real server load on `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` revision `905e84b50c4d2a365ebde34e685027578e6728db` (A800-80GB) with a Gemma 4 PEFT adapter whose layer-15 attention carries `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`o_proj` but no `v_proj` (the reporter's adapter from https://github.com/nemilentsau/sglang-gemma4-triton-fallback):

Only Gemma 4 is exercised end to end; the other models are covered by the additive, skip-only nature of the `should_apply_lora` gate rather than by new E2E runs. The reporter adapter targets attention only, so the symmetric k-fill path and the double-wide MLP dims are covered by the unit test `test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_qkv_normalization.py` (4 cases).

+def _zero_fill_kv_branch(weight_name, q_weight, base_hf_config):
+    """Build a zero tensor for a missing K/V LoRA branch when both are absent.
+
+    A lora_A shares q_proj's input width, but a lora_B's output width is the KV
+    projection size, which is smaller than q_proj under GQA. Derive it from the
+    base attention config; fall back to q_proj's shape when unavailable.
+    """
+    if "lora_B" not in weight_name:
+        return torch.zeros_like(q_weight)
+    if base_hf_config is not None and hasattr(base_hf_config, "get_text_config"):
+        base_hf_config = base_hf_config.get_text_config()
+    num_heads = getattr(base_hf_config, "num_attention_heads", None)
+    num_kv_heads = getattr(base_hf_config, "num_key_value_heads", num_heads)
+    if not num_heads or not num_kv_heads or num_heads == num_kv_heads:
+        return torch.zeros_like(q_weight)
+    kv_out = q_weight.shape[0] // num_heads * num_kv_heads
+    return torch.zeros(
+        (kv_out, *q_weight.shape[1:]),
+        dtype=q_weight.dtype,
+        device=q_weight.device,
+    )
+

+"""Unit tests for LoRA qkv normalization and Gemma 4 native-LoRA buffer dims.
+
+Regression coverage for #25913: a Gemma 4 E2B PEFT adapter whose KV-sharing
+layers carry q/k/o weights but omit v_proj used to crash LoRAAdapter loading,
+and the Gemma 4 multimodal LoRA buffer dims were computed with a single
+head_dim for every layer. CPU-only.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.lora.lora import LoRAAdapter
+from sglang.srt.models.gemma4_mm import Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestLoRAQKVNormalization(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_missing_v_proj_is_zero_filled_from_k_shape(self):
+        q_name = "base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.15.self_attn.q_proj.lora_A.weight"
+        k_name = q_name.replace("q_proj", "k_proj")
+        qkv_name = q_name.replace("q_proj", "qkv_proj")
+        weights = {
+            q_name: torch.ones(2, 3),
+            k_name: torch.full((2, 3), 2.0),
+        }
+
+        LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj(None, list(weights), weights)
+
+        self.assertEqual(set(weights), {qkv_name})
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][0:2], torch.ones(2, 3)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][2:4], torch.full((2, 3), 2.0)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][4:6], torch.zeros(2, 3)))
+
+    def test_missing_k_and_v_use_kv_width_for_lora_b_under_gqa(self):
+        # Adapter with only q_proj on a GQA layer: both K and V are zero-filled,
+        # and a lora_B must use the KV output width (num_kv_heads*head_dim), not
+        # q's wider output, or the stacked qkv_proj lora_B has the wrong shape.
+        q_name = "base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.3.self_attn.q_proj.lora_B.weight"
+        qkv_name = q_name.replace("q_proj", "qkv_proj")
+        weights = {q_name: torch.ones(8, 2)}  # q_out = num_heads(4) * head_dim(2)
+        fake_self = SimpleNamespace(
+            base_hf_config=SimpleNamespace(num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=1)
+        )
+
+        LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj(fake_self, list(weights), weights)
+
+        # kv_out = num_kv_heads(1) * head_dim(2) = 2; qkv = 8 + 2 + 2
+        self.assertEqual(set(weights), {qkv_name})
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(weights[qkv_name].shape), (12, 2))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][0:8], torch.ones(8, 2)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][8:12], torch.zeros(4, 2)))
+
+    def test_missing_k_proj_is_zero_filled_from_v_shape(self):
+        q_name = "base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.7.self_attn.q_proj.lora_B.weight"
+        v_name = q_name.replace("q_proj", "v_proj")
+        qkv_name = q_name.replace("q_proj", "qkv_proj")
+        weights = {
+            q_name: torch.ones(8, 2),
+            v_name: torch.full((3, 2), 4.0),
+        }
+
+        LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj(None, list(weights), weights)
+
+        self.assertEqual(set(weights), {qkv_name})
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][0:8], torch.ones(8, 2)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][8:11], torch.zeros(3, 2)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[qkv_name][11:14], torch.full((3, 2), 4.0)))
+
+
+class TestGemma4LoRADimensions(CustomTestCase):
+    def _make_model(self):
+        text_config = SimpleNamespace(
+            hidden_size=1536,
+            head_dim=256,
+            global_head_dim=512,
+            swa_head_dim=256,
+            num_attention_heads=8,
+            num_key_value_heads=1,
+            intermediate_size=6144,
+            num_hidden_layers=2,
+            num_kv_shared_layers=1,
+            use_double_wide_mlp=True,
+            layer_types=["sliding_attention", "full_attention"],
+        )
+        config = SimpleNamespace(get_text_config=lambda: text_config)
+        model = Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.__new__(Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration)
+        model.config = config
+        return model
+
+    def test_sliding_attention_lora_dims_use_swa_head_dim(self):
+        model = self._make_model()
+
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("qkv_proj", 0), (1536, 2560))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("o_proj", 0), (2048, 1536))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("gate_up_proj", 0), (1536, 12288))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("down_proj", 0), (6144, 1536))
+
+    def test_full_attention_lora_dims_use_global_head_dim_and_double_wide_mlp(self):
+        model = self._make_model()
+
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("qkv_proj", 1), (1536, 5120))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("o_proj", 1), (4096, 1536))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("gate_up_proj", 1), (1536, 24576))
+        self.assertEqual(model.get_hidden_dim("down_proj", 1), (12288, 1536))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Under Grouped Query Attention (GQA), the output dimension of q_proj is different from k_proj and v_proj. If both k_proj and v_proj are missing from the adapter, falling back to weights[q_name] for zero-filling will produce weights with the wrong shape (matching Q instead of KV), leading to shape mismatches and runtime errors. We should compute the correct KV output dimension using the base model's attention configuration when lora_B is being normalized.

```python

                    num_kv_heads = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "num_key_value_heads", num_heads) if self is not None and hasattr(self, "base_hf_config") else 1

                        head_dim = getattr(self.base_hf_config, "head_dim", hidden_size // num_heads)

                            (num_kv_heads * head_dim, weights[q_name].shape[1]),
                            dtype=weights[q_name].dtype,
                            device=weights[q_name].device,
```

+            if should_apply_lora is not None and not should_apply_lora(module_name):
+                continue

issue_comments.body:
I tried this branch with a PEFT adapter trained on gemma-4-31B-it and it still fails there, for two reasons that do not show up on E2B:

1. The 31B adapter has v_proj on the 50 sliding layers and no v_proj on the 10 full-attention layers (`attention_k_eq_v`). `normalize_qkv_proj` still decides adapter-wide whether v_proj exists, so it raises the same `KeyError` on layer 5. The new test only covers an adapter with no v_proj anywhere.
2. 31B has `num_global_key_value_heads=4` vs `num_key_value_heads=16`. `get_hidden_dim` uses the global count for every layer, so on sliding layers it allocates a 10240-wide qkv buffer for a 16384-wide tensor. This is the gap @anshulkulhari7 flagged as latent; on 31B it is live.

I also hit a third problem once those two were fixed: PEFT adapters trained on the VLM can carry vision-tower tensors, and `LoRAAdapter` buckets by layer index, so `vision_tower.encoder.layers.N.self_attn.o_proj` overwrote the language o_proj for layer N.

I put the fixes plus a CPU test with the 31B shapes in #40964, on top of the same three changes as this PR, and checked it against HF+PEFT logprobs on the real model. Happy to fold anything back here instead if you would rather land it in this PR.

Thanks @Yash-Sawant22 for running this against a real 31B adapter and confirming the per-layer KV-head sizing gap is live there — that's exactly the asymmetry I flagged in review (`get_hidden_dim` using the global `num_key_value_heads` for every layer while the base `qkv_proj` uses `swa_num_key_value_heads` on sliding layers), and the `getattr(..., "swa_num_key_value_heads", ...)` fallback in #40964 is the same shape I suggested. All three issues stem from treating the adapter as uniform — per-layer presence/sizing for the first two, module-path bucketing for the vision-tower/language `o_proj` collision — so they belong together in that fix. No preference on venue from my side: whichever PR the maintainers want to land it through works, and the 31B-shape CPU test you added is worth keeping either way.

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for Gemma 4 multimodal LoRA configurations, updates QKV normalization to handle missing projection branches by zero-filling them, and adds a `should_apply_lora` check during module initialization. It also includes comprehensive unit tests for these changes. The review feedback highlights two critical issues: first, under Grouped Query Attention (GQA), falling back to the Q-projection shape for zero-filling when both K and V projections are missing will cause shape mismatches; second, the new `should_apply_lora` gate will inadvertently skip LoRA for FusedMoE layers on MoE models, requiring special handling for these layers.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

Thanks for this — it's a careful, well-targeted fix, and the LoRA-side reasoning is genuinely subtle and correct. I read through the diff against `main` (`9bb9d17`) and traced the buffer/slice paths; my overall take is **approve-with-nits**: the core fix is right, the regression test locks in the important case, and the only thing actually keeping it red is a missing CI label, not the code. One real latent correctness gap on a Gemma-4 variant is worth a look but doesn't block the reported #25913 case.

### `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora.py` — the GQA KV zero-fill is exactly right

The both-missing KV-width derivation in `_zero_fill_kv_branch` is subtle but correct. A `q_proj` `lora_B` has out-dim `num_attention_heads * head_dim`, so `q_weight.shape[0] // num_heads` recovers `head_dim` and `* num_kv_heads` gives `num_kv_heads * head_dim` — the true K/V projection width. Deriving `head_dim` from the actual tensor shape rather than a config field is the right call for Gemma, where `head_dim * num_heads != hidden_size` (`head_dim=256`). The `"lora_B" not in weight_name -> zeros_like(q)` short-circuit is also correct, since q/k/v `lora_A` are all `(r, hidden_size)` and thus shape-identical regardless of GQA, and the `num_heads == num_kv_heads` MHA fast-path is correct (KV width == Q width there). This properly addresses the gemini-code-assist GQA concern for the q_proj-only / both-KV-missing case, and `test_missing_k_and_v_use_kv_width_for_lora_b_under_gqa` asserts the V slice is zero at the KV width — which would fail if q's wider output were used — so it actually locks the behavior in. The rewritten `normalize_qkv_proj` (popping k/v only when present, reusing v's shape for missing-k and `zeros_like(k_proj_weight)` for missing-v) is clean and the three test cases cover all three branches.

### `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py` — load-bearing dead-gate fix

This is the quiet but important one. On `main`, `should_apply_lora` is defined on 13 model classes (the VL/audio multimodal models) but has **zero call sites** — the only non-`def` references are the comment at lines 776-778, which already says "before the should_apply_lora gate" even though no gate existed yet. So the method was dead, and every module whose leaf name matched `target_modules` (including vision/audio tower projections) was being wrapped as a LoRA layer. Wiring it via `getattr(self.base_model, "should_apply_lora", None)` is exactly right: text-only models that don't define it get a clean `None` no-op, and the gate is strictly skip-only so it can never wrongly *include* a module. I confirmed the gemma4 `lora_pattern` is anchored on `^language_model\.layers\.`, so `language_model.layers.N.self_attn.qkv_proj` matches while `vision_tower`/`audio_tower`/`embed_vision`/`embed_audio` prefixes don't — towers correctly excluded. Nice catch.

One test-gap note (non-blocking): this gate is now the behavioral core of the lora_manager change, but the new CPU test only exercises `normalize_qkv_proj` and `get_hidden_dim` — nothing touches `init_lora_modules`, and the tower-exclusion is validated only by the single gemma4 E2E run in the description. If it's feasible without a real module map, a small unit test stubbing a `base_model` whose `should_apply_lora` returns `False` for a `vision_tower.*` name and `True` for a `language_model.layers.N.self_attn.qkv_proj` name (then asserting `init_lora_modules` skips the former) would lock the regression in.

### `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py` — root-cause fix is right; one asymmetric-KV gap

Routing `get_hidden_dim` through `get_text_config()` is the right root-cause fix: it reads dims from the same normalized `text_config` that the config normalization mutates (swapping in `global_head_dim` for full-attention, planting `swa_head_dim`) and that the actual `Gemma4TextModel` is built from — instead of the top-level `Gemma4Config` that lacks `intermediate_size` and the per-layer attn dims. The per-layer `head_dim` split (global vs `swa_head_dim`) and the double-wide-MLP tail are handled correctly.

One real latent gap worth a look: `get_hidden_dim` now picks `head_dim` per layer, but the `qkv_proj` branch still uses the **global** `text_config.num_key_value_heads` for *every* layer. The base `qkv_proj` layer uses `swa_num_key_value_heads` on sliding layers (`gemma4_causal.py:308`), and these two diverge whenever `num_global_key_value_heads` is set (`hf_transformers/config.py:167-179`: `num_key_value_heads` becomes the global count, `swa_num_key_value_heads` keeps the raw/sliding count). The LoRA-B buffer is allocated per layer from this `output_dim`, and `slice_lora_b_weights` then slices using the base layer's per-layer KV shard size — so on a Gemma-4 variant where `num_global_key_value_heads != num_key_value_heads`, the sliding-layer qkv buffer width won't match `q + 2*kv` and you'd get a shape error at load. The fix is currently asymmetric: per-layer for `head_dim`, global for the KV-head count. Suggest mirroring the model in the non-`full_attention` branch: `num_kv_heads = getattr(text_config, "swa_num_key_value_heads", text_config.num_key_value_heads)`. This is latent on E2B (equal global/swa KV counts, which is why E2E passes), and the new test uses `num_key_value_heads=1` for both layers so it doesn't exercise it. (`o_proj` is fine since it uses `num_attention_heads`, which is constant across layers.)

### What unblocks this (CI)

The red checks are **not** a real failure. Every failing check is the `run-ci` label gate in `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`: the job exits 1 unless the PR carries the `run-ci` label, and the `*-finish` jobs only go red because they aggregate that gate. This PR currently carries only the `lora` label, so **no actual test/build job has executed** — every GPU/CPU matrix shows `skipping`. That means the new CPU test (`test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_qkv_normalization.py`, registered to `base-a-test-cpu`) hasn't actually run in CI yet, so the current green-ish bits aren't "tests pass." A maintainer needs to add the `run-ci` label to trigger the suites and confirm the new CPU test passes before merge — as an external contributor the author can't add the label or self-trigger.

The repro in the PR body (manual server run + local pytest) is solid; a `run-ci` pass would close the loop. Nice work overall.

The one real follow-up I flagged inline — the per-layer `swa_num_key_value_heads` count in `gemma4_mm.get_hidden_dim` — is latent on E2B and doesn't block #25913.
